questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'CANDID':
questions.explanation: C is correct. Candid = frank, honest, straightforward. Its antonym = evasive (deliberately vague, avoiding direct answers). Options B and D are synonyms of candid. Option A (truthful) is also close to candid — all three wrong options are near-synonyms of the given word, a classic exam trap.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'FRUGAL':
questions.explanation: A is correct. Frugal = careful about spending; avoiding waste; economical. Its antonym = extravagant (spending more than necessary; wasteful). Options C and D are near-synonyms of frugal. Option B (careful) also aligns with frugal.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'LETHARGIC':
questions.explanation: D is correct. Lethargic = sluggish, lacking energy or enthusiasm; drowsy. Its antonym = energetic (full of energy and enthusiasm). Options A, B, C are all related to the meaning of lethargic — the question tests careful elimination.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'SERENE':
questions.explanation: B is correct. Serene = calm, peaceful, undisturbed. Its antonym = agitated (troubled, disturbed, anxious). Options A, C, D are all synonyms of serene. Agitated is the clear opposite in meaning and emotional state.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'COVERT':
questions.explanation: C is correct. Covert = not openly acknowledged; secret; hidden. Its antonym = overt (done openly, not secret). Example: 'overt racism' = racism displayed openly; 'covert operation' = secret mission. Options A, B, D are all synonyms of covert.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'PROLIFIC':
questions.explanation: A is correct. Prolific = producing a great quantity; highly productive (a prolific author = writes many books; prolific farmland = yields much produce). Its antonym = barren (producing little or nothing; unproductive). Options C and D are synonyms of prolific. Option B (creative) is partially related but doesn't capture the quantity/productivity meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'PRUDENT':
questions.explanation: D is correct. Prudent = acting with careful thought and good judgment; cautious. Its antonym = reckless (acting without thought for the consequences; careless). Options A, B, C are all near-synonyms of prudent. This is a trap question — students may choose D too quickly and then second-guess themselves.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'AUSTERE':
questions.explanation: B is correct. Austere = severe or strict in manner; simple and without comfort; self-disciplined and unindulgent. Its antonym = lavish (sumptuously rich, elaborate, and expensive; generous to excess). Options A, C, D overlap with aspects of austere (strict, harsh, simple) and are not antonyms.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'BENEVOLENT':
questions.explanation: C is correct. Benevolent = well-meaning and kindly; desiring to do good. Its antonym = malevolent (having or showing a wish to do evil to others). The 'bene-' prefix means good; 'male-' means bad/evil. Options A, B, D are all synonyms of benevolent. The root-based contrast (bene vs. male) makes this a classic vocabulary pair.

questions.stem: Choose the word MOST OPPOSITE in meaning to 'VERBOSE':
questions.explanation: D is correct. Verbose = using more words than necessary; wordy. Its antonym = succinct (briefly and clearly expressed; concise). Synonyms of verbose include: long-winded, talkative, prolix, garrulous — all three wrong options. Synonyms of succinct include: laconic, terse, pithy, brief.
